title: SEO or Google Ads first? What each costs a GTA business
excerpt: SEO vs Google Ads for a GTA small business: published Toronto retainers, 2026 click costs, time to first lead, and how to split under $2,000 a month.
keywords: SEO vs Google Ads cost, how much does SEO cost Toronto, SEO or PPC small business, how long does SEO take, Toronto SEO retainer, Google Ads cost Canada 2026
intro_html:
You have maybe $1,500 a month for marketing and two salespeople telling you different things. The SEO agency says ads are rented traffic that stops the day you stop paying. The ads agency says SEO is six months of invoices before a single call. Both are partly right, and neither tells you what the other one costs.

This is a neutral comparison for a GTA owner with under $2,000 a month: published Toronto SEO retainers, Google Ads click costs for Canada, how long each takes to produce a lead, and a month-by-month way to split a small budget. Every figure was checked against its source page on October 10, 2026, and the dates of older surveys are given so you can weigh them.

sections.heading: What Toronto SEO retainers actually cost
sections.body_html:
Toronto agencies that publish prices cluster in two bands. SEO24 lists Starter at $1,000 a month (two articles and three local citations), Growth at $2,000 and Enterprise at $3,500, with no long-term lock-in, and says typical Toronto ranges run from about $1,000 to $2,500 a month for focused local campaigns. SEO Partners Toronto starts its Local package at $2,500 a month for two long articles, three referring domains and a Google Business Profile rebuild with eight posts a month; Growth is $4,500 and Competitive starts at $7,500, all month to month. Seologist (updated June 2026) publishes ranges instead: $180 to $400 an hour and retainers of $2,500 to $15,000 a month. All three quote Canadian dollars.

Two older surveys give a sanity check. Ahrefs polled 439 providers (updated August 2024): the most common retainer was $501 to $1,000 a month, and agencies averaged $3,209 a month against $1,348.63 for freelancers. SE Ranking surveyed 260 agencies (December 2024): 22% of US and Canadian respondents charge over $2,000 a month, and 70% had raised prices or planned to. Those are US dollars; at the Bank of Canada's October 9 rate of 1.4271, the agency average is about C$4,580 (my conversion).
sections.takeaway: Budget $1,000 to $2,500 a month for a real local SEO retainer in the GTA. Under $1,000, you are usually buying a freelancer's hours, not a program.

sections.heading: What Google Ads costs: clicks plus management
sections.body_html:
Google Ads has two costs, and quotes often hide one. The first is the clicks. Google's help page on CPC bidding says you pay for each click, you set a maximum, and you are often charged less. Consultus Digital's September 2026 guide gives planning ranges for Canadian accounts: $4 to $12 a click for home services with $1,500 to $5,000 a month to compete, $3 to $10 for dental, $8 to $30 or more for legal, and $0.50 to $3 for retail. A GTA home-services advertiser, it adds, can pay two to three times what the same business pays in a mid-sized Ontario city. For a cross-check, LocaliQ's 2026 search benchmarks (June 2026, US campaigns) put the average click at US$5.42 and the average lead at US$66.69, about C$95, with home improvement at US$90.92 a lead and dentists at US$72.97.

The second cost is management. Consultus lists three Canadian models: 10% to 20% of ad spend, sometimes with a minimum; a flat $400 to $2,500 a month; or $100 to $200 an hour. We went deeper in our post on Google Ads management fees. A $1,000 ad budget with a $500 fee is really $1,500, and only two-thirds of it buys clicks.
sections.takeaway: Add the management fee to the click budget before comparing with an SEO quote. A $1,000 ad budget is rarely a $1,000 month.

sections.heading: Time to first lead: tomorrow versus months
sections.body_html:
Ads start when the budget does. Google's page on average daily budgets says you can set and edit the budget at any time, with a monthly limit of 30.4 times the daily amount. If your landing page and tracking are ready, a search campaign can take calls on day one.

SEO is slower, and Google says so. In its "How to Hire an SEO" video, Google's Maile Ohye said that in most cases SEOs need four months to a year to implement improvements and then see a potential benefit, a line Semrush quotes in its own guide. Google's current "Do you need an SEO?" page (updated June 2026) tells you to ask any provider what results to expect and in what timeframe, and warns that no one can guarantee a number-one ranking. When Ahrefs polled 3,680 people (January 2024), the typical answer was three to six months.

One more reason SEO is the longer bet: Seer Interactive tracked 3,119 informational queries across 42 organizations from June 2024 to September 2025 and found organic click-through of 0.61% when an AI Overview appeared, against 1.62% when it did not. Local service searches are less affected than how-to questions, but write for the customer, not the summary box.
sections.takeaway: If you need calls this month, only ads can deliver them. Start SEO expecting the first measurable gain at month four or later.

sections.heading: The free SEO every new site should ship with
sections.body_html:
Before you pay anyone a retainer, do the parts Google documents for free.

  • Claim your Business Profile. Google's Business Profile page says creating one and listing on Search and Maps is free. Its local ranking help page says results are ranked on relevance, distance and prominence, and states plainly that there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking.
  • Get the details right. Whitespark's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors (published November 2025) ranks the primary profile category first, proximity to the searcher second, keywords in the business title third, a physical address in the city of search fourth, and being open at the time of search fifth. Review and behavioural signals are gaining weight; citations keep slipping.
  • Fix the on-page basics. Google's SEO starter guide (updated December 2025) asks for a unique, clear and concise title, a short page-specific meta description, descriptive URLs, alt text on images and a Search Console account, and notes that most new pages Google finds are discovered through links.

What stops when you stop paying? With ads, everything: pause the campaign and the calls end. With SEO, the pages, profile and reviews stay, but rankings drift as competitors keep publishing. Neither is permanent; one just fades slower.
sections.takeaway: A complete Business Profile and a site built to the starter guide cost nothing but an afternoon, and they are where most GTA service searches are won.

sections.heading: How to split under $2,000 a month over six months
sections.body_html:
This is my example, not a rule. Take $1,500 a month and a one-location service business.

  • Months 1 and 2: free basics, then ads. Ship the Business Profile and starter-guide fixes yourself in week one. Put the whole $1,500 into one Google Search campaign, roughly $1,000 of clicks plus management, with call and form tracking on from day one. At $4 to $12 a click that is 80 to 250 clicks a month, enough to learn which searches turn into booked jobs.
  • Months 3 and 4: trim ads, start content. Cut the search terms that never convert and hold ads at about $1,000. Spend the remaining $500 on two pages a month written around the searches that did convert, which is close to what the $1,000 SEO tier above buys, or a freelancer at the Ahrefs median.
  • Months 5 and 6: judge both on the same number. Compare cost per booked job, not clicks or rankings. If organic calls have started, shift $250 a month from ads to SEO. If not, keep the ads and ask the SEO provider what changed in the timeframe they promised.

Who should skip SEO for now: anyone who needs cash flow this month, a seasonal trade entering its peak, or a business about to rebuild its website, since Google's hiring guide says a redesign is the moment to bring an SEO in. Who should skip ads: a business whose clicks cost more than the margin on a first job, or one with no page worth sending a click to.
sections.takeaway: Ads first for cash flow, free SEO on day one, paid SEO once you know which searches book. Decide at month six on cost per job.

bottom_line_html:
In the GTA, a focused local SEO retainer runs $1,000 to $2,500 a month and takes four months or more to show a benefit. Google Ads costs a few dollars to a few tens of dollars a click plus a management fee, and can ring the phone tomorrow. With under $2,000 a month, run one search campaign first, do the free SEO yourself, and buy paid SEO only once you know which searches turn into jobs.

faq.q: How much does SEO cost per month in Toronto?
faq.a: Toronto agencies that publish prices start local plans at about $1,000 a month, and the common range for a focused local campaign is $1,000 to $2,500. One agency's local tier starts at $2,500, and published ranges run to $15,000 a month for large sites. Below $1,000 you are usually buying a freelancer's hours rather than a monthly program. Figures are Canadian dollars as checked in October 2026.

faq.q: Is SEO or Google Ads cheaper for a small business?
faq.a: Per month they can cost the same, around $1,500, but they buy different things. Google Ads buys clicks now, at roughly $4 to $12 each for GTA home services plus a management fee. SEO buys pages, profile work and links that take months to pay off but keep working after the invoice. Judge both on cost per booked job after six months, not on clicks or rankings.

faq.q: How long does SEO take to get results?
faq.a: Google's own guidance is four months to a year to implement improvements and see a potential benefit, and an Ahrefs poll of 3,680 people put the typical answer at three to six months. Small edits can show in days, but ranking changes usually take weeks to months. If a provider promises a number-one ranking by a fixed date, Google says to be wary.

faq.q: Can I do local SEO myself for free?
faq.a: The highest-impact parts, yes. A Google Business Profile is free, Google says there is no way to pay for a better local ranking, and Whitespark's 2026 factors put the primary category, proximity, business title, address and opening hours at the top. Add Google's starter-guide basics such as clear page titles, meta descriptions and Search Console. Paid SEO adds content and links on top of that base.
